detailLevel: actionable. HEIC decode is an explicit operator choice via env toggle, default off. This delivery supports off and the production-proven external vips mode; an in-process global-libvips mode is deferred to a separate future feature.
description: Give PhotoDesk the ability to actually decode and edit iPhone HEIC originals on the HomeServer production host, not just fail safely on them. HomeServer runs Linux Mint 22.1 (xia) and hosts both PhotoDesk and Immich. Today the editor renders from the Immich /original buffer through the prebuilt Sharp binary (src/edit-renderer.js, src/routes/api.js). Sharp's prebuilt binaries intentionally omit HEIC/HEVC decode (patent-encumbered; only royalty-free AVIF/AV1 is bundled), so every iPhone HEIC original currently lands in the safe-failure path with a 'HEIC decode failed on this host' error. This feature provisions a real HEVC decode path on the target host, validates it against representative iPhone fixtures, and preserves the existing non-destructive, safe-failure guarantees as a hard constraint.
designReference: No new UI surface. The existing editor, EDITED badge, and the render_error display path (src/routes/api.js HEIC branch) are reused. Any new copy must use the shipped dark-only tokens and Review language.
targetPlatform: HomeServer: Linux Mint 22.1 (xia), running PhotoDesk and Immich through the existing git-deploy + systemd flow documented in deploy/ and planning/database-and-deployment.md. HomeServer is the authoritative production target and its real installed tooling may be used for production validation. The current development checkout runs on macOS with Homebrew vips 8.18.3; local results are useful for development but do not replace validation on HomeServer. Generic Debian-family portability remains desirable but is secondary. x64 glibc is the primary production arch; macOS development and ARM64 builds must not be assumed to match production behavior.
knownTargetFacts: HomeServer (Linux Mint 22.1 xia) has apt libvips-tools at vips-8.15.1 (confirmed via `vips --version`).

The current development host is macOS with Homebrew vips 8.18.3. Its library version and build features differ from HomeServer, so successful local decode or integration tests are not production capability evidence.
Implication for libvips mode: 8.15.1 is below Sharp 0.34's required libvips (~8.17), so libvips mode REQUIRES a from-source libvips build. This is settled, not speculative.

External mode is PROVEN on HomeServer with zero extra packages. `vips -l | grep heif` showed heifload compiled in, and `vips copy IMG_0001.heic IMG_0001.tif` on a real iPhone HEIC succeeded: a 1.3MB HEVC-coded HEIC decoded to a 36MB uncompressed TIFF, confirming the HEVC decoder is wired into the installed apt vips. No libheif-plugin-libde265/libde265 install was needed.

End-to-end external mode is PROVEN on HomeServer with PATH auto-discovery and only PHOTODESK_HEIC_DECODE=external configured: an iPhone HEIC was edited, rendered, uploaded to Immich, and the uploaded result was confirmed.
Net recommendation is now firm: implement off + external first; external requires no new packages on HomeServer. libvips mode remains optional/later and is the only path needing a from-source build.
rootCause: Sharp prebuilt input formats are JPEG/PNG/WebP/AVIF/TIFF/GIF/SVG only; HEIC is excluded by design. Decoding iPhone HEIC (HEVC-coded) requires libvips compiled with libheif + an HEVC decoder (libde265). The current host 'advertises HEIF input' (libheif present for the AVIF/HEIF container) but cannot decode HEVC, which is exactly the observed 11.6003 failure.
principles: HEIC decode is an operator choice, default off. PhotoDesk ships and runs normally with no HEIC support; an operator opts in explicitly via env. Nothing about HEIC is attempted unless a mode is enabled. This matches PhotoDesk not yet being wired into homebase automation.

Safe-failure is non-negotiable: whatever decode path lands, an unsupported, disabled, or broken host must still leave originals untouched, keep the previous ready edit usable, and surface an actionable compatibility error. This is a regression-tested constraint, not a nice-to-have.

Decode fidelity must be full-resolution. Rendering edits from Immich's downsized preview (getThumbnailBuffer, size=preview) is not an acceptable primary path; it may only exist as an explicitly-labeled degraded fallback if at all.
Capability must be proven by a real decode, never inferred from sharp.format metadata. progress.txt already records this lesson: codec presence is not proof of decodability.
Originals are never mutated; edited derivatives remain JPEG, stacked into Immich on Commit, consistent with Feature 3/4.

Deployment must stay reproducible on HomeServer's Linux Mint 22.1 environment via the existing git-deploy + systemd flow. A maintainer should be able to reproduce the working HEIC setup from documentation alone; generic Debian-family notes are secondary and must not replace validation on HomeServer.
EXIF capture metadata and correct display orientation must survive into the rendered JPEG derivative.

envToggles.summary: HEIC decode behavior is selected entirely by env, default off, so an operator opts in and picks a strategy explicitly. The code must treat 'off' as the safe baseline and never attempt HEIC work unless a mode is enabled.

vars.name: PHOTODESK_HEIC_DECODE
vars.meaning: off = current behavior, no decode attempted. external = out-of-process system vips decode into a bounded temporary TIFF before the existing Sharp render pipeline.

vars.name: PHOTODESK_HEIC_DECODER_CMD
vars.values: absolute path to the decoder binary (external mode only)
vars.default: auto-detected: heif-convert, else vips, else unset
vars.meaning: Lets the operator point at the exact CLI used in external mode rather than relying on PATH discovery.

envToggles.validation: On boot, an enabled mode whose tooling/capability is missing must NOT crash the app: log an actionable error, report capability as unavailable, and fall back to safe-failure for HEIC while normal editing continues. 'off' performs no probing.

openDecisions.question: Which HEIC mode is delivered first?
openDecisions.decision: Deliver off + external only. Global-libvips is deferred until a separate feature supplies reproducible source-build and deployment automation.

schemaPlan.migration: None required. This feature reuses the existing edits table (render_status, render_error) and adds no columns. If a capability-cache table is later desired it should be a separate, optional migration.

stories.title: HEIC decode mode env toggle, default off
stories.summary: Introduce PHOTODESK_HEIC_DECODE (off|external) and PHOTODESK_HEIC_DECODER_CMD with off as the safe default.
acceptanceCriteria: src/config.js reads and validates the new env vars; an unknown value fails closed to 'off' with a logged warning.
With PHOTODESK_HEIC_DECODE unset or off, no HEIC decode is attempted and behavior is byte-for-byte the current safe-failure path.
The selected mode is observable via the /api/edits/capabilities response (mode plus proven decode status from HEIC-003).
An enabled mode with missing tooling does not crash the app: it logs an actionable error, reports the mode as unavailable, and continues serving non-HEIC editing.
The env vars are documented in .env.example and the README/deployment docs.

stories.title: External server HEVC decode capability documented and verified
stories.summary: Keep HomeServer external-mode decoding reproducible with copy-pasteable setup and preflight checks.
acceptanceCriteria: Docs record HomeServer's exact external-mode setup: Linux Mint 22.1 (xia), vips 8.15.1, and the proven `vips copy` command, including verification commands for heifload and a real fixture.
Following the documented steps for whichever mode is enabled yields successful decode of a real iPhone HEIC fixture on a fresh server.

stories.title: Real-decode startup capability check
stories.summary: Replace metadata-based capability inference with a check that actually decodes a bundled HEIC fixture at startup/deploy and reports pass/fail.
acceptanceCriteria: When PHOTODESK_HEIC_DECODE is off, the check is skipped entirely and capabilities report mode=off (no probing).
When a mode is enabled, on boot (or via a deploy preflight command) PhotoDesk attempts a real decode+render of a small committed HEIC fixture through that mode and records the result.
sharpCapabilities()/the /api/edits/capabilities endpoint reports heicDecode as proven-by-decode for the active mode, not derived from sharp.format.heif fileSuffix.
When an enabled mode fails the decode, the check logs an actionable message pointing at the deployment doc for that mode, and the app still starts and serves non-HEIC editing normally.
The check does not meaningfully slow normal startup (fixture is small; result may be cached for the process lifetime).

stories.title: HEIC render path integrated into the editor pipeline
stories.summary: Wire the enabled decode mode into renderEditBuffer/writeRenderedEdit so saving an edit on a HEIC original produces a correct JPEG derivative. The render path dispatches on PHOTODESK_HEIC_DECODE.
acceptanceCriteria: With a mode enabled, saving an edit on a HEIC original produces a correct, full-resolution JPEG with crop and adjustments applied, matching the live preview within documented tolerance.
Display orientation is correct exactly once (no double-rotation across the external-mode decode boundary).
ICC handling preserves a sensible color result (Display P3 input is not silently mangled).
EXIF capture metadata (datetime, and GPS where present) is preserved into the derivative, sourced from the original/Immich asset info rather than a lossy intermediate.
Per-asset edit serialization, atomic temp-then-rename writes, and previous-ready preservation from Feature 3 remain intact.
In external mode: subprocess failures and aborts remove the temp intermediate and do not leave partial files.
Mode dispatch is isolated (e.g. a decode-source helper) so adding/removing a mode does not touch the adjustment/crop pipeline.

stories.title: Safe-failure preserved and regression-tested
stories.summary: Guarantee that mode=off, an unconfigured mode, or a broken/failed decode still degrades exactly as today, and lock it with a regression test.
acceptanceCriteria: When mode is off, decode capability is absent, or a HEIC decode throws, the original is never modified and any previous ready edit remains usable.
The user sees the actionable HEIC compatibility error (existing render_error surface), not corrupt output.

A regression test covers both mode=off and an enabled-but-failing mode, asserting: previous-ready edit preserved, render_status/render_error correct, and a 422 with an actionable message — mirroring the current src/routes/api.js HEIC branch behavior.

stories.title: iPhone HEIC fixtures and validation tests
stories.summary: Acquire and commit representative iPhone HEIC fixtures and add decode/orientation/metadata assertions.
acceptanceCriteria: Small synthetic HEVC-coded fixtures are committed under test/ for fast startup and orientation checks.

A location-scrubbed real tiled iPhone HEIC approved for repository use is committed as test/fixtures/test.heic and used by integration tests, including coverage for files that exceed libheif's default item-reference security limit.
A test asserts a rotated iPhone HEIC renders upright (orientation correctness), since HEIC orientation is a common silent-rotation bug.
A test asserts the rendered derivative dimensions/crop bounds and deterministic file creation, consistent with the Feature 3 JPEG fixture test.

backendDependencies: Immich /original asset download (getOriginalAssetBuffer) and getAssetInfo (for EXIF/orientation) are already proxied server-side.
external mode: an apt-provided libheif/libvips CLI decoder (heif-convert from libheif-examples, or vips/vipsthumbnail from libvips-tools) plus a temp-file working area; apt-only, no compile.
PHOTODESK_EDIT_DIR remains the durable output location; any HEIC intermediate must use a temp area that is cleaned on success and failure.
researchNeeded: For external mode, the decoder availability question is settled on HomeServer: installed vips 8.15.1 successfully decodes the real iPhone fixture. Still verify ICC preservation and orientation behavior through the application pipeline.
Determine whether iPhone HEIC EXIF/orientation is more reliably sourced from Immich getAssetInfo than from the decode boundary.
Verify Immich upload/stack flow is unaffected by HEIC-derived JPEGs (should be identical to existing JPEG derivatives, but confirm).
outOfScope: HEVC/HEIC ENCODE or writing HEIC output (we only decode; derivatives stay JPEG).
Bounded-memory streaming rewrite (P2 item) beyond the temp-file hygiene that external mode naturally introduces.
Any change to the editor UI/adjustment model.
Multi-arch/musl/Alpine support beyond keeping ARM64 buildable.
In-process global-libvips mode and its source-build provisioning; track as a separate future feature.
implementationSlice: Ship PHOTODESK_HEIC_DECODE=off|external, prove external vips with real fixtures at startup/deploy, integrate bounded serialized decode into the render path, preserve safe failure and required Immich metadata, and validate on HomeServer.
